description: Mapping the Urban Heat Island in Oklahoma City is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. To address the issue of extreme heat, federal partners created the National Integrated Heat Health Information System (NIHHIS), a division of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). Starting in 2017, NIHHIS began funding Climate Adaptation Planning + Analytics (CAPA) Strategies to support more than 70 UHI mapping campaigns. Coverage: Oklahoma City (2023). The toolkit gives Oklahoma City as the location, 2023 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
